feature: KDE Plasma Wayland automatic application profile switching
status: Focus-source and runtime-boundary feasibility demonstrated; production integration not implemented
recommended_path: Temporary per-session KWin script reports foreground PID and window identity over session D-Bus
Host-side observer authenticates KWin sender and resolves same-user /proc executable with PID-reuse checks
Host-side observer applies existing debounce, G HUB exclusion and installation-aware Wine path mapping
Existing private atomic token-bound mailbox crosses into Wine runtime
Existing pinned agent-local adapter emits original typed application event; G HUB matcher and automatic-profile policy remain authoritative

critical_finding.observation: pressure-vessel --share-pid exposes process IDs, but /proc/<desktop-pid>/exe returns EACCES across its user namespace in the isolated test
critical_finding.consequence: Keep executable resolution outside the Wine runtime user namespace for both packaged X11 and Wayland; sharing process IDs alone is insufficient
critical_finding.current_x11_scope: Existing workstation X11 installation is manually accepted. Newly packaged runtime profile path has not had full E2E validation and must address this boundary before qualification
critical_finding.workaround_tested: The host observer resolves the executable successfully and the container reads the existing mailbox payload correctly
critical_finding.no_permission_widening: No CAP_SYS_PTRACE grant, ptrace policy change, EIS allowlist edit or global input permission bypass

implementation_constraints: Use the actual launch session bus. Verify org.kde.KWin owner and expected session; never assume an inherited SSH/xrdp bus is correct.
Load a session-unique script from a private path visible to host KWin, outside container-private /tmp; do not persistently enable scripts in kwinrc.
Run observer in the host user namespace. Reuse process_identity and wine_path; preserve container /run/host path translation when feeding G HUB.
Production transport should use libdbus or another existing runtime dependency; Qt6 development tools in this research fixture must not become installation prerequisites.
Supervise host observer with existing agent readiness and shutdown lifecycle, with stale heartbeat detection and bounded cleanup.
On KWin owner change, discard old events, reset script epoch and reconnect with initial current-focus snapshot. Do not retain objects/PIDs across compositor restart.
Handle lock/unlock explicitly, suspend switching on session/identity loss, and resample focus on recovery. Preserve current profile during G HUB UI focus.
Keep per-session token, sequence validation, private directory permissions and atomic writes across the host/container handoff.

alternatives.x11_observer_only: Insufficient for native Wayland clients; use compositor focus rather than Xwayland root properties.
alternatives.standard_ext_foreign_toplevel_list: Protocol supplies title/app_id/identifier, but no focus-state or PID event; insufficient by itself for current executable matching.
alternatives.new_Wine_Wayland_driver: No evidence that this is required; focus source can change while retaining tested Wine X11/Xwayland rendering and input.

remaining_acceptance: Implement and package host-side observer supervision for both launcher families; current source deliberately keeps Wayland profile observer disabled.
Complete Wayland G HUB E2E with distinct native app profiles, automatic on/off, unmatched-app Desktop fallback, own-window exclusion and real mapped keys.
Test lock/unlock, rapid focus changes, observer failure, compositor restart and orderly shutdown.
Run packaged path on Manjaro and CachyOS; then Bazzite with SELinux enforcing.
Flatpak identities, foreign Wine/Proton prefixes and non-KWin compositors remain unqualified.
experiment_notes: Initial local probe hit NVIDIA EGL loading in a GPU-less namespace. Final probe pins Mesa/llvmpipe only inside that disposable environment; no host driver setting changed.
KWin wrapper restarts a failed session. Harness now records result then exits inner session successfully, and propagates failure from the outer harness to preserve evidence.
Disposable materialized Linux runtime is removed after boundary probe; source runtime is read-only except a private overlay of its empty reference lock.
